characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy governs the design, scoping, and execution of non-production demonstrators that validate platform-neutral or fallback authentication options. It defines the experimental paths (e.g., FIDO2 on GrapheneOS, browser-based fallback, or DID-based passwordless schemes), sets success criteria (interoperability with OpenID Connect, resilience under network partition, measurable costs), and tracks risks (timeline, budget, credential protection). It translates technical feasibility into policy-ready evidence, informs procurement considerations, and benchmarks against standards such as NSIS/eIDAS. The lever's success is evidenced by built demonstrators, formal feasibility findings, a risk register, and a credible cost/benefit analysis linked to procurement negotiations.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Key positive interactions include feeding concrete demonstrator results into Policy Advocacy Strategy, bolstering arguments for resilience and continuity; and strengthening Procurement Influence Strategy by providing credible, cost-aware technical capabilities that procurement can cite in supplier-neutral language. It also supports EU Standards Engagement Strategy by validating standards-based FIDO2/OpenID implementations.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include budget and schedule pressures; concentrating on a narrow demonstrator scope can slow coalition-building efforts and create friction with Coalition Building Strategy. It may also constrain EU Standards Engagement Strategy by narrowing alignment opportunities for alternative standards and by limiting breadth of stakeholder input during critical early-phase decisions.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy shapes the political and regulatory environment for platform-neutral access and fallback authentication by translating technical findings into policy propositions, stakeholder messaging, and procurement expectations. It coordinates with Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, the MitID operator, and parliament committees to frame resilience, continuity of service, supplier concentration risk, and procurement neutrality as policy priorities. Immediate deliverables include formal policy proposals and coalition-facing materials; systemic impact is measured by higher likelihood of AltID requirements reflecting platform-neutral language (target ~20% shift); strategic impact is broader adoption of resilient, interoperable standards across procurement and EU dialogue.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Coalition Building Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy: broad coalitions supply credible policy proposals and diverse inputs, while EU-focused engagement aligns messaging with cross-border standards. Collaboration also amplifies Technical Feasibility Strategy by ensuring demonstrator results reach diverse stakeholder groups.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy can conflict with Procurement Influence Strategy if policy messages push for broad openness while procurement demands tighter risk controls. It may also clash with Coalition Building when messaging polarizes stakeholders or slows consensus. Regulatory inertia or conflicting political agendas can slow policy adoption despite evidence.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy scales advocacy by mobilizing a broad network of stakeholders across civil society, privacy advocates, academic researchers, security experts, contingency planners, and sympathetic members of Folketinget's digital policy committee. It sets engagement approaches, governance norms, and conflict-resolution pathways to maintain alignment while incorporating diverse perspectives. Immediate impact: increased stakeholder engagement; systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions; strategic: greater political pressure for platform neutrality and resilient authentication. The lever manages trade-offs between speed and breadth, ensuring that technical feasibility and policy aims are translated into coherent, widely supported actions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Policy Advocacy Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy: broad coalitions supply credible policy proposals and diverse inputs, while EU-focused engagement aligns messaging with cross-border standards. Collaboration also amplifies Technical Feasibility Strategy by ensuring demonstrator results reach diverse stakeholder groups.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: The Coalition Building Strategy can conflict with rapid, centralized decision-making if diverse voices pull in conflicting directions; it may slow consensus on demonstrator scope and procurement language. It also risks diluting focus from Procurement Influence Strategy if coalition demands competing priorities that dilute platform-neutral commitments.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy aims to embed platform-neutral language and certified fallback mechanisms in AltID-related procurement documents, while promoting supplier diversity and resilience. It operationalizes the governance of platform risk into contract terms, objective evaluation criteria, and procurement scoring that reward reduced vendor lock-in. Immediate: platform-neutral language included in procurement documents; systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated diversity; strategic: long-term dependency reduction on Apple/Google. It must balance enforceability, supplier pushback, and alignment with EU standards and policy proposals.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Best synergy with Technical Feasibility Strategy and Policy Advocacy Strategy: demonstrators and policy proposals give procurement teams concrete, standards-aligned terms to contract; robust fallback concepts support platform-neutral messaging, while coalition-backed advocacy fuels acceptance of procurement changes. It also aligns with EU Standards Engagement Strategy to harmonize cross-border purchases.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Procurement Influence Strategy can conflict with Coalition Building Strategy if procurement terms favor quick, non-diverse suppliers over broader coalition demands; it may also provoke pushback from incumbents resisting platform-neutral requirements, creating political and legal friction. Tension may arise with EU Standards Engagement Strategy if harmonization pressures clash with national procurement autonomy.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy coordinates Danish advocacy with European bodies, technical working groups, and wallet initiatives to influence interoperability, portability, resilience, and vendor neutrality. It monitors eIDAS2, NSIS, and European Digital Identity Wallet developments, provides formal input, drafts position papers, and orchestrates EU-level consultation responses. It seeks to ensure that platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms are embedded in European artifacts, while accommodating national procurement realities. Deliverables include EU-facing standards input, alignment with AltID goals, and a pathway to meshing Danish policy with broader Digital Identity Wallet frameworks.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Key positive interactions are with Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy: EU-level input strengthens national policy proposals and procurement terms toward cross-border interoperability, while alignment with EU standards magnifies the credibility of platform-neutral demands within Danish governance. This also complements Coalition Building Strategy by broadening stakeholder legitimacy.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy can conflict with national sovereignty if EU discourse imposes timelines or requirements that clash with Danish procurement cycles; it may also complicate Coalition Building when EU-driven positions diverge from domestic coalition priorities. It can strain resources as engagement consumes budgets that otherwise support national pilots.
